why: Both notes are accurate on every number and page. A adds the citation inconsistency and the missing latency and cost. B adds the WS precision overclaim and the uninitialized-backbone inconsistency. These strengths roughly balance.

only_here: Cross-batch sampling is cited inconsistently: [23] RocketQA on p.1 and [30] Wang et al. on p.2
Flags the 'massive real-world impact / millions of additional products' claim as unsupported by any table
Lists latency and serving cost of GTE-base vs DistilBERT as not reported
Notes that absolute metric values are absent
Notes that no public benchmark is used
WS does not actually recover precision: +2.01% is still below DistilBERT+DR+CB+HHN at +2.09%, contrary to the paper's 'recovered' claim
The 'uninitialized backbone' wording conflicts with GTE-base starting from a public checkpoint
Clarifies that the abstract's +7.34% NDCG@5 comes from human review, not offline metrics
Notes that D=8 GPUs, so the pool grows only about 8x, linearly
Notes that WS is not tested on DistilBERT and CB/HHN are not tested without DR
Notes that no cross-encoder accuracy is reported
